call_operation.description: Call an operation of any imported API through Jentic One's broker, which checks the agent's permission rules, adds the stored credential and records the call. The workflow never holds the API's key.
call_operation.name: call_operation

parameters.description: The operation: its id from 'Search for an API operation' (op_...), or its method and address, such as GET https://api.example.com/v1/items/{id}.
parameters.name: operation

parameters.description: Values for the {placeholders} in the operation's address, such as {"id": "123"}.
parameters.name: path_parameters

parameters.description: Inputs sent after the '?' in the address, such as {"limit": 10}.
parameters.name: query_parameters

parameters.description: The request body. An object or a list is sent as JSON; text is sent as it is.
parameters.name: body

parameters.description: Extra headers for the API. Leave out authorization: Jentic adds the stored credential itself.
parameters.name: headers

parameters.description: Which credential to use, when several cover the same API: pick it, or enter its name. On Jentic One 0.39, which groups credentials into toolkits, pick the toolkit. Leave empty to let Jentic choose.
parameters.name: credential

parameters.description: Any unique text. Jentic answers a repeat of the same call with the same key for a day from its record, rather than calling the API twice. It keeps a repeated answer's body only up to 256 KB.
parameters.name: idempotency_key

parameters.description: What to do when the API answers with an error status. Continuing lets later steps check the status themselves, which suits a 404 that just means not found.
parameters.name: on_error

api_vendor.description: The vendor of the API called.

body.description: What the API sent back: JSON as data, text as text.

body_base64.description: A body that is neither JSON nor text, such as an image, base64-encoded.

body_omitted.description: Whether a replayed answer comes without its body, because Jentic keeps bodies only up to 256 KB for replays.

content_type.description: The type of what the API sent back.

credential_id.description: The stored credential Jentic signed the call with.

execution_id.description: Jentic's record of this call. 'Get an execution record' reads it.

headers.description: The API's response headers, names in lower case.

operation.description: The call that was made: its method and full address.

operation_id.description: Jentic's id for the operation called.

replayed.description: Whether this is the first answer again, replayed for a repeated idempotency key instead of calling the API.

status.description: The HTTP status the API answered with.

toolkit_id.description: On Jentic One 0.39: the toolkit the call went through.

get_agent_access.description: See what this connection can reach in Jentic One: the agent's credentials (or its toolkits, on Jentic One 0.39), the APIs they serve, its scopes, and where calls are sent. Changes nothing, so it also makes a good first step for checking the connection.
get_agent_access.name: get_agent_access

agent_id.description: The agent this connection acts as.

apis_served.description: Every API the agent can call, as ids for 'Search for an API operation'.

can_call_apis.description: Whether it may call APIs through the broker.

credentials.description: The stored credentials bound to the agent. Empty on Jentic One 0.39, which binds toolkits instead.

bound_at.description: When it was bound to the agent.

serves.description: The APIs it signs calls to. A missing name or version covers them all.

api_id.description: The API as vendor/name/version, the form every Jentic step takes.

vendor.description: Who publishes the API, as Jentic spells it.

status.description: active, or disabled if it has been switched off.

toolkits.description: On Jentic One 0.39: the toolkits bound to the agent.

bound_at.description: When it was bound to the agent.

serves.description: The APIs its credentials sign calls to.

api_id.description: The API as vendor/name/version, the form every Jentic step takes.

vendor.description: Who publishes the API, as Jentic spells it.

warning.description: Why the instance's own details are missing, if they are.

get_background_job.description: See whether a background job has finished, such as an import still running when its step ended, and get what it produced: the imported APIs for an import, the API's answer for a call.
get_background_job.name: get_background_job

parameters.description: The job's id, as 'Import an API from the catalog' gave it back.
parameters.name: job_id

apis.description: For a finished import: the APIs it added.

api_id.description: The API as vendor/name/version, the form every Jentic step takes.

host.description: The host its operations are called on.

revision_id.description: The revision of the API's description that is live.

state.description: The revision's state, such as imported. Empty for an API that was already imported.

vendor.description: Who publishes the API, as Jentic spells it.

body.description: For a finished call: what the API sent back.

body_base64.description: A body that is neither JSON nor text, base64-encoded.

content_type.description: The type of what the API sent back.

error.description: What went wrong, including why a call never reached the API. A job still running can carry one while it retries.

execution_id.description: For a call: Jentic's record of it.

is_finished.description: Whether nothing more will happen to it.

kind.description: import for an import, execution for a queued call.

ok.description: For a finished call: whether that status is 2xx, false when the call never reached the API.

status.description: queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled or dead_letter, or unchanged for an import that found the API already up to date.

status_code.description: For a finished call: the HTTP status the API answered with.

get_execution.description: Read Jentic One's record of a brokered call: whether it succeeded, the status the API answered with, how long it took and which credential signed it. Bodies are not kept.
get_execution.name: get_execution

parameters.description: The record's id, as 'Call an API operation' gave it back.
parameters.name: execution_id

actor_id.description: The agent or person who made it.

api_id.description: The API as vendor/name/version, the form every Jentic step takes.

host.description: The host its operations are called on.

vendor.description: Who publishes the API, as Jentic spells it.

duration_ms.description: How long the call took, in milliseconds.

error.description: What went wrong, when the call failed.

http_status.description: The HTTP status the API answered with.

origin.description: How it was made: api, mcp, cli, dashboard, agent or system.

trace_id.description: The trace id, for matching against logs.

get_operation.description: Read everything an operation takes before calling it: the placeholders in its address, its query and header inputs and the body it expects, each marked required or not.
get_operation.name: get_operation

parameters.description: The operation: its id from 'Search for an API operation' (op_...), or its method and address, such as GET https://api.example.com/v1/items/{id}.
parameters.name: operation

body.description: The request body it takes, if any.

description.description: What the API says it is.

schema.description: Its JSON Schema, such as its type.

path_parameters.description: Inputs that fill the {placeholders} in the address.

description.description: What the API says it is.

schema.description: Its JSON Schema, such as its type.

description.description: What the API says it is.

schema.description: Its JSON Schema, such as its type.

server.description: The base address the API is served from.

url.description: The upstream address, with {placeholders} for path inputs.

import_catalog_api.description: Import an API from Jentic's public catalog so its operations can be searched and called. An API already imported, with nothing newer in the catalog, is left as it is. Calling it still needs a credential for it bound to the agent in the console, through a toolkit on Jentic One 0.39.
import_catalog_api.display_name: Import an API from the catalog
import_catalog_api.name: import_catalog_api

parameters.description: The API's catalog id, such as httpbin.org or googleapis.com/gmail. 'Search the API catalog' gives it.
parameters.name: api_id

parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the import to finish. A longer import hands back its job to check later.
parameters.name: wait_seconds

already_imported.description: Whether the catalog had nothing newer to import.

apis.description: The imported APIs; pass an api_id to the other steps.

api_id.description: The API as vendor/name/version, the form every Jentic step takes.

host.description: The host its operations are called on.

revision_id.description: The revision of the API's description that is live.

state.description: The revision's state, such as imported. Empty for an API that was already imported.

vendor.description: Who publishes the API, as Jentic spells it.

job_id.description: The import job, when one ran. 'Check a background job' follows it.

status.description: completed, unchanged when it was already imported, or the job's status if it is still running.

list_api_operations.description: List every operation of one imported API: its method, path, summary and id, ready to pass to 'Call an API operation'.
list_api_operations.name: list_api_operations

parameters.description: The imported API, as vendor/name/version. 'List imported APIs' gives each one's id.
parameters.name: api

parameters.description: The most operations to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The previous step's 'next_cursor', to get the next page.
parameters.name: cursor

has_more.description: Whether more results follow this page.

next_cursor.description: Pass this as 'Continue from' in the same step to get the next page.

deprecated.description: Whether the API marks it deprecated.

operation_id.description: Jentic's id for it; 'Call an API operation' takes it.

path.description: Its path on the API's server.

list_apis.description: List the APIs imported into Jentic One, each with the id the other steps take, its number of operations, how it authenticates, and whether the catalog has a newer description.
list_apis.display_str_template: List the APIs imported into Jentic.
list_apis.name: list_apis

api_id.description: The API as vendor/name/version, the form every Jentic step takes.

catalog_api_id.description: Its id in the catalog, when it came from there.

current_revision_id.description: The revision of its description that is live.

display_name.description: The name shown in the console, where one is set.

host.description: The host its operations are called on.

origin.description: catalog when it came from Jentic's catalog.

security_schemes.description: How the API authenticates, such as apiKey or oauth2.

list_executions.name: list_executions

parameters.description: An API's name or domain, such as stripe or googleapis.com. Leave empty to browse.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: The most APIs to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The previous step's 'next_cursor', to get the next page.
parameters.name: cursor

api_id.description: Its catalog id; 'Import an API from the catalog' takes it.

github_url.description: Its page in Jentic's public API repository.

update_available.description: Whether the imported copy is out of date.
